sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Balch Springs, TX?
sections.html:
A Balch Springs homeowner can list the house, sell it directly to a person, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is and closes on a date the seller picks. Which route works best depends on the house's condition, any liens or code notices on it, and how soon the money has to arrive.

Homeownership is common here. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates show 64.7 percent of housing units occupied by their owners, and 3.29 people per household. Many sales in a community like this involve family homes held for years, inherited houses, or rentals that an owner no longer wants to manage.

  • Traditional listing: works when the house shows well and the buyer's lender can approve it.
  • Direct sale to an investor: skips showings and loan approval, and usually skips repairs.
  • Selling with a plan for liens: payoff of a mortgage, tax balance or code fine comes out of the proceeds at closing, so get each figure in writing first.

sections.h2: What is the history of Balch Springs, and how does it shape its housing?
sections.html:
Balch Springs began as a cluster of farms around a spring and became a commuter suburb of Dallas, which is why most of its houses date from the postwar decades. The Texas State Historical Association says the community was founded around 1870 when the family of John Balch settled by three springs, one of which never ran dry.

Residents incorporated the town on June 13, 1953, with a mayor-council government, in order to avoid annexation by Dallas. The population was about 3,500 in 1956, 13,050 by 1976, 17,406 in 1990 and 19,375 in 2000. Interstate 635 made the drive to Dallas faster in the 1970s, and by the late 1970s about 95 percent of working residents commuted to Dallas or Garland.

The town sits on Interstates 635 and 20 and U.S. Highway 175, ten miles southeast of Dallas in Dallas County. Hickory Creek rises here. By 1991 the town had seventeen manufacturers, including makers of shipping pallets and machine parts. In 1988 residents voted to combine with Mesquite, but the vote was ruled invalid and Balch Springs remained independent. In earlier decades children attended school in either the Dallas or Mesquite districts, so ask the county appraisal district which school district taxes your parcel today.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Balch Springs homes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Balch Springs was valued at $224,400 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and median gross rent was $1,378. The July 1, 2025 population estimate of 27,258 is 1.6 percent below the 2020 estimates base of 27,705, though it is above the 23,728 counted in 2010.

With 9.02 square miles and 3,067.9 people per square mile, the city is compact. About 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and a 33.7 minute average commute is a reminder that many owners work elsewhere in the Dallas area.

sections.h2: Does Balch Springs require rental registration or a certificate of occupancy?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's permit requirements sheet lists both a rental registration and a certificate of occupancy, and a seller with a tenant or an investor buyer should expect to deal with each.

  • Rental registration: the applicant needs a driver's license and proof of ownership, such as closing paperwork or a deed in the applicant's name. The registration must be renewed every two years.
  • Inspection timing: the city says rental inspections must be done before a tenant moves in, or the owner incurs a violation fee.
  • Certificate of occupancy: the applicant provides a driver's license, a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan.

Because registration is tied to the owner's name and deed, a buyer who plans to rent the house will register in their own name after closing. Contact the Permits and Inspections Division at 972-286-4477 to ask what is on file for your address. Inspection requests are sent by email to inspections@balchspringstx.gov, per the city's permits page.

sections.h2: How does Balch Springs code enforcement work, and can an open violation block a sale?
sections.html:
An open violation does not stop a sale, but it follows the property and usually has to be cleared or priced into the deal. Balch Springs code officers survey neighborhoods daily and also respond to complaints.

A first violation notice gives the owner 10 days to comply, or 7 days for high grass and solid waste. A notice stays valid for 12 months. If a re-inspection shows the problem remains, the officer issues a Notice to Appear citation that names the ordinance, the fine and how to schedule a court date. The department also takes extension requests when more time is needed to finish a repair.

Before you list or sign a contract, walk the property and compare it with the city's Top 10 code violations list, which the Code Enforcement page links in English and Spanish. Tell a buyer about any citation or court date so the closing is not delayed by a surprise.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on my mortgage in Balch Springs?
sections.html:
Texas lets lenders foreclose without going to court on most home loans, but the process runs on fixed notice periods, and selling before the auction is often possible. Federal rules generally bar a servicer from starting foreclosure until the loan is more than 120 days delinquent.

  • After a notice of default, you can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of receiving it.
  • At least 21 days before the sale, the servicer must send a notice of sale, post it at the courthouse door and file it with the county clerk.
  • Sales are public auctions on the first Tuesday of a month, held between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. at the place the commissioners court designated.
  • After a sale, the lender may sue for a deficiency within two years, and the borrower can ask for a fair market value offset.

The commissioners court of Dallas County, where Balch Springs sits, designates the sale area, so ask the county clerk where auctions are held. Selling the house before the first Tuesday can pay off the loan from the proceeds, and the Texas State Law Library's foreclosure guide lays out each step.

sections.h2: What should I know if tenants live in the house?
sections.html:
Give every buyer a copy of the lease, because its terms decide what the new owner can and cannot do about the tenant. If you need the tenant out before closing, Texas requires a written notice to vacate, normally at least three days unless the lease sets a different period.

If the tenant stays, the eviction suit is filed in justice court, the tenant must be served at least four days before trial, and a hearing is set between 10 and 21 days after filing. A losing party can appeal to county court within five days of judgment. A writ of possession cannot issue until six days after final judgment. Many sellers with tenants choose a buyer who will take the house with the tenant in place, which avoids that timeline.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental before I sell my Balch Springs house?
faqs.a: Registration is the owner's duty while the house is rented, and it must be renewed every two years with an inspection before a tenant moves in. A buyer who keeps the house as a rental registers under their own name with proof of ownership after closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to fix a code violation in Balch Springs?
faqs.a: The first notice gives 10 days, and 7 days for high grass or solid waste. The notice stays valid for 12 months, and if the problem is still there after a re-inspection, the officer issues a citation with a fine and a court date. You can request an extension from the department.

faqs.q: Which county records the deed on a Balch Springs sale?
faqs.a: Balch Springs lies in Dallas County, so the Dallas County clerk records deeds for properties in the city. Recording requires a signed deed acknowledged before a notary or another officer authorized to take acknowledgments.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Balch Springs house after a foreclosure notice?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the sale closes before the auction. You have 20 days from the notice of default to reinstate, and the lender must give at least 21 days' notice of sale. Sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month, so count back from that date.

faqs.q: How many people live in Balch Springs?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 27,258 residents on July 1, 2025, living in 8,247 households counted in the 2020-2024 survey. The estimate is 1.6 percent below the 2020 estimates base, and the city covers 9.02 square miles.
